implementation_notes: Express makes the split implicit but complete: app.get('/users/:id', handler) registers one callback per route (the Action) and the res object is the Responder - res.status(404).json({...}) sets status, headers and body in a single call; the domain must be a module or function that never receives req. A separate responder object is not idiomatic here because res already is one; extract a response-mapping module when the same handler result must be rendered as JSON, HTML and CSV, otherwise keep the handler thin and end it in exactly one res call. Node's raw http module gives the same shape at a lower level with ServerResponse.
pitfalls: Express 4 does not catch rejected promises from async handlers: without next(err) (or Express 5) the request hangs on an unhandled rejection.
Calling res.send/res.json twice throws ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT; make the branches that can answer mutually exclusive and return after each.
Middleware that mutates req.body or res.locals becomes hidden action input, so the handler is no longer testable from its arguments alone.
